Generated background plates: FLUX.1 Depth [dev] test on the orange scene

Session impl, 2026-10-30 (brief from prim before 13:51; this page 18:01). Design: RES, docs/TEMPORAL_TEXTURE_CONSISTENCY.html §4e/§4f. Scene: res31's runs/real2sim/v1/orange (read-only). All numbers from new code are UNVERIFIED until the checker passes them.

Verdict. Yes, a depth-conditioned image model can make a usable exterior plate for this scene on our 8 GB laptop GPU.
  • FLUX.1 Depth [dev] (NF4) made three 1280×720 plates from the sim's empty-scene depth, about 109 s each.
  • In two of the three, the table lines up with the sim table almost exactly: walnut 98% and white 95% of the table outline within 3 px. The real LaMa plate manages 9%, because the real table isn't where the sim table is.
  • The object check rejects one plate, white: a small fixture on its tabletop reads as a "block".
  • res31's light fit cannot run on a still, so the composites reuse the real scene's light.
  • Not tested: whether GR00T acts the same on these plates. That's out of scope and needs its own go.
Licence. FLUX.1 [dev] is under the FLUX.1 [dev] Non-Commercial licence (accepted on HF by the user, 10-30), and the plates inherit it. Fine for this research test; flag it before any other use.

2 · Method

  1. Empty-scene depth (CPU), experiments/genplate/render_empty.py, .venvs/real2sim, osmesa.
    • MuJoCo renders scene.mjb from its calibrated ext camera (1280×720) with the robot and all movable objects hidden. Only the floor plane and the table box remain.
    • Control image: disparity 1/z mapped to 0–255. Anything beyond 3 m is set to 0, because the floor plane runs out to 102 m and would otherwise flatten the table.
    • Aspect: generated at the camera's own 1280×720, with no crop or pad.
  2. Plates (GPU, prim's lock), experiments/genplate/gen_flux.py, .venvs/flux.
    • Model: transformer and T5 from diffusers/FLUX.1-Depth-dev-nf4; VAE, CLIP and tokenizers from black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Depth-dev.
    • 28 steps, guidance 10, seed 0, one prompt per plate.
    • Three processes: embed, then denoise, then decode, so the VAE and the transformer are never on the GPU together (see §4).
  3. Compare (CPU), experiments/genplate/compare.py, importing res31's composite and perceive read-only.
    • Objects: Grounding DINO, using perceive's defaults and the scene's nouns (block, bowl). A hit centred on the sim table rejects the plate.
    • Edges: the sim table outline (image-border pixels dropped, 1,525 px) against Canny edges of the plate. The measure is the share of outline pixels within 3 / 10 px of a plate edge.
    • Composites: composite.Compositor(m, scene, plate), the same replay qpos at review frames 0, 37, 63, 75, 100 and 126 for every plate.

Prompts:

  • oak: "a photo of an empty light oak wooden workbench in a robotics lab, plain white wall behind, nothing on the table, soft indoor ceiling light, realistic"
  • white: "a photo of an empty white laminate table in a bright office, light grey wall behind, nothing on the table, diffuse daylight from a window, realistic"
  • walnut: "a photo of an empty dark walnut wooden table in a kitchen, beige tiled wall behind, nothing on the table, warm indoor light, realistic"

Reading the numbers:

  • Oak's 53% is mostly the measure, not the plate. Its right-hand table edge is pale against a pale floor, and Canny misses it; by eye the edge sits on the outline (§3a).
  • LaMa's 9% is a real geometry gap. The sim table doesn't cover the real table at the near-left corner, and its right edge doesn't follow the real one. The generated plates don't have this gap, because they're drawn to the sim's geometry.

3c · Light fit

res31's calibrate_light.py can't run on a generated plate. It fits the light by matching the real robot's shadow across video frames, and a still plate has no robot. So the composites reuse the real scene's light.json for both the shadow direction and its strength (real shadow ratio). Each generated plate has its own painted light, such as the window patch on white, and nothing checks that it agrees with the sim shadows. A still-image light fit would be new work and needs a go; that question goes to res31.

5 · Problems met, and fixes

  • HF token. The brief said robotics_agentic/.env, but that file holds only NIM keys. The cached HF login was used instead; it is never printed or committed.
  • GPU busy check. A resident system process, launch_vst (86 MiB), is always listed by nvidia-smi. Changed to prim's rule: total GPU memory used ≤ 500 MiB.
  • OOM 1: the VAE and the transformer were on the GPU together. Fixed by splitting them; the pipeline skips its own encode when the control arrives already packed.
  • OOM 2: the transformer wasn't freed before the decode. Fixed: the decode runs in its own process, each latent is saved to disk at once, and gc.collect() runs before empty_cache.
  • Segfault in compare.py: in .venvs/real2sim, importing Triton (through torchvision when Grounding DINO loads) after mujoco crashes with signal 11. Fixed in my script only by importing Triton first. Which native library clashes is not established. res31 may hit the same thing if their code ever loads Grounding DINO after MuJoCo.
  • RAM contention: the download briefly pushed MemAvailable under prim's floor while TaskGen's GR00T A/B was running, and TaskGen paused itself. CPU work was then held until TaskGen finished.

6 · Limitations

  • The background is invented. The sim has no walls, so FLUX picks the room: a lab hall, an office, a kitchen. The sim floor plane becomes a visible floor, and the camera now looks into a large open room rather than at a near wall as in the real scene.
  • Light is not matched. The shadows come from the real scene's fitted light, while each plate paints its own lighting. Nothing measures whether they agree (§3c).
  • The edge measure undercounts low-contrast edges (oak). It is a pixel measure on one camera, with fixed Canny thresholds.
  • The object check is a detector at perceive's default thresholds. It caught a fixture as a "block" (correct to reject) and a LaMa smudge as a "bowl". It will miss objects it has no noun for. Background clutter off the table (oak) isn't rejected.
  • One scene, one seed, three prompts. There's no estimate of how often a plate fails.
  • No policy check. We don't know whether GR00T-DROID acts the same on a generated plate as on the real one (the distribution-shift risk in §4e). That's the next test that matters, and it needs a separate go.
  • Control latent: the depth control is encoded with the VAE's mode, not a random sample as in the stock pipeline. It's deterministic, and the effect is expected to be negligible, but that hasn't been tested.
  • Non-Commercial licence on the model and the plates.
